quote: Home Assistant does not use a consumption sensor directly. It calculates consumption for each hour like this:
text:
This is almost always a mapping issue in the Energy dashboard rather than the EG4 itself, and the fact that HA shows roughly double (88.5 kWh vs 41.1 kWh in EG4) is the classic clue that something is being counted twice.

Home Assistant does not use a consumption sensor directly. It calculates consumption for each hour like this:

consumption = grid import + solar production + battery discharge - grid export - battery charge

So your idea is close, but grid export does need to be in there. If exported energy is not subtracted, consumption will look too high on any day you send power back to the grid.

I would check these in order under Settings > Dashboards > Energy:

Grid supply and Grid return are two separate energy sensors. Grid supply should only ever increase when you import, and Grid return should only increase when you export. If one net sensor is used in both places, or the export sensor is missing, the calculation breaks.

Solar production is gross PV production for the day, before it is split into home use, battery charging, and export. With EG4 systems a common mistake is picking an inverter AC output or load/EPS sensor that already includes battery discharge. That will double-count the battery.

Battery has separate charge and discharge energy sensors, both in kWh. Charge is energy into the battery, discharge is energy out of the battery. If the integration reports a single signed or net battery sensor it will not work correctly in the dashboard.

Every sensor used there should be an energy sensor in kWh with a total-increasing behaviour over the day. If any of them are power sensors in W, or daily sensors that reset at a different time than the EG4 app, the daily totals will not line up. If the EG4 integration only gives you power, you need integral helpers for each flow and they all need the same method.

A quick way to find the culprit is to pick one sunny hour in History and do the maths by hand. Note the increase in that hour for import, export, so

quote: The problem is that your energy sensor is reporting 0 instead of unavailable when it is unavailable.
text:
The problem is that your energy sensor is reporting 0 instead of unavailable when it is unavailable. i.e. The states act like this:

Total → 0 → Total = add the entire total to the energy dashboard

Total → unavailable → Total = no change.

If you are using template sensors this can be fixed with an availability template.

If you are using some integration for your energy sensors you can report this issue to the developer of the integration. If you have no luck there you can filter your sensors through a template sensor.

Please show your sensor configuration rather than the customizations of your sensors.

Also please do not post pictures of text. Post the actual text and format it correctly for the forum. That goes a long way in helping us help you, as we can then copy/paste/edit the configuration to guide you to a solution.

quote: Make sure your integral helpers are using method: left.
text:
Looks like you have the correct sensors in place. Though instead of naming them “Output Power kWh” you should name them “Energy” to prevent confusion. Power and energy are different things.

Can you share the history graph for the solar energy sensor?

Other things to check:

Make sure your integral helpers are using method: left. This will reduce approximation errors for data that has sharp transitions.

Check the solar energy sensor in Developer Tools → Statistics. Click the ramp icon to the right and then the OULIERS button. Also fix any issues that are indicated.
